subject.title: Import Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter captures into the canonical local store

question: Should Birdclaw adopt third-party passive-capture files as a supported durable data source, and if so should the first contract be limited to Scrollmark canonical bundle v1?
rationale: Code can reuse existing canonical persistence, but maintainers must choose the supported producer/version boundary and approve provenance, completeness, account ownership, migration, and backup semantics before implementation.

options.title: Start with Scrollmark v1
options.body: Support only the versioned canonical bundle initially and require explicit provenance and partial-collection semantics before considering legacy formats.

options.title: Design a generic capture importer
options.body: Approve both producers together behind a shared normalized envelope, accepting broader compatibility and fixture-maintenance costs.

options.title: Defer external capture support
options.body: Keep official archives and Birdclaw-controlled live transports as the only supported ingestion sources for now.

recommendation.title: Start with Scrollmark v1
recommendation.body: Support only the versioned canonical bundle initially and require explicit provenance and partial-collection semantics before considering legacy formats.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice governs Birdclaw's product scope and durable storage contract, both anchored in VISION.md and the existing import architecture.
